Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
WOODEN CONES FOR WINDING YARN 

0. FOREWORD 

O.l This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 30 June 19G9, after the draft finalized by the Textile Mill Accessories 
( Other Than Jute ) Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile 
Division Council. 

0,2 In formulating' this standard, due weightage has been given to the 
international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevailing in 
the field in this country. Considerable assistance has been derived from 
the following publications: 

ISO/R 325-1963 ( E ) Wood cones for cross winding ( half angle of the 
cone 4"^ 20'), International Organization for Standardization. 

ISO/R 326-1963 (E) Wood cones for cross winding (nominal half 
angle of the cone 5"^ 57' ), International Organization for Standard- 
ization. 

ISO/R 327-1963 (K) Wood cones for cross winding (half angle of the 
cone 3^ 30'). International Oiganization for Standardization. 

B.S. 2547:1960 Cones and tubes for winding textile yarns, British 
Standards Institution. 

0.3 This standard contains' clauses 3.2,1, 4.3 and8.3 and Note under Table 1 
which rail for agreement betw<'en the buyer and the seller for permit- 
ting him to use his option for selection to suit his rec\niremcni^, 

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with> the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded olT in accordance with 
IS: 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded 
oflT value shall be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes requirements for and method of sampling of 
wooden cones for winding yarn (cross-wound ). 



*Rule3 for rounding off numerical value* ( revised), 

2 



IS: 5141 -1969 

1.2 This standard covers cones having the following angles: 

a) 3" 30', 

b) 4' 20', and 

c) 5' 57'. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the angle of cone shall mean the angle 
contained between the side and the axis, that is, half the total angle, 

3. MANUFACTURE 

3.1 Material — The cones should be manufactured from well-seasoned 

limber, 

NoTK 1 - — A list of recommended species of limber is given m Appendix A for 
information of the manufactmer. 

NoTK 2 — ^ A recommended code of manufacturing blanks for cones is also given in 
Appendix A, 

3.2 Finish — The cones shall have a smooth finish. 

3.2,1 If prescribed by the buyer, grooves shall be provided at the base 
to accommodate tail ends of yarn, 

Note — Such grooves are provided only if (he cones are to be used in magazine 
creel. 

3.3 Freedom from Defects — The cones should be Uc^ from bark pockets, 
checks or cracks, gum ducts, honeycombing, knots, splits and other defects 
which are likely to affect the life or usefuhiess of the cones. For the 
description of various types of defects, sfe IS: 707*1968*. 

4. REQUIREMENTS 

4.1 Dimensions — The cones depending upon their angle shall conform to 
the requirements of Table 1 when read wiih Fig, 1, 

4.2 Concentricity - -Clones shall be concentric. The eccentricity of cones 
shall, howevtT, not exceed the values given below: 

Base — 0'25 mm 
Top — 0^'7r) mm 

4.3 Weight — The average weight of a cone in a lot shall be as agreed to 
between the buyer and the seller. A tolerance of ±4 percent on the con- 
tracted weight shall, however, be permissible.

6. MARKING 



6.1 Each cone shall be marked at a sniial>]o place with tho angle of cone 
and brand or trade-mark of the mamilacturer. 

6*2 BIS Certiflcution Marking 

The producl may al^^o be marked wiih Standard Mark. 

6.2.1 The use of ihe Standard Mark is governed by (he provisions of 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and (he Ruk\s and Regulations made 
thereunder. The details of conditions under which the hcencc for the use of 
Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

7, PACKING 

7.1 Cones shall l)e packed in wooden cases strong enough to withstand 
normal hazards of storage and transport,. 

7.2 Each pack or case of cones shall bear the followhig information: 

a) Manufacturer's name, mitiais or trade-maik, if any; 

b) Number of cones packed; 

c) Desii^nation of cones [see 5*1 ); and 

d) Year of manufacture. 

8, SAMPLING 

8.1 Lot — The quantity of cones of same designation and manufactured 
from the sam<i spei ies of timbei delivered fn a buyer jgainst a despatch 
note shall constitute a lot. 

8.2 'J'iie conformity of the lot to tlie requirements of tliis specification shall 
be determined on ilie basis of thi^ tests ranit^d out on the samples selected 
fiom It. 

8.3 Unless otherwise at^reed to betv^een the buyer and the seller the num- 
ber f)f cdues to t)e selected tit random Uom a lot shall be according to 
Table 2, 

8.4 The cones selected according to 8.3 shall be examined for finish^ 
freedom from delects, dimensions, (on(entntity and wejt^ht, 

8.5 Criteria for Conformity — The lot shall be declared c(mforming to the 
requirements of the specification il the number ol" cones not satisfying the 
lequirements for any one or more of die c haiacteristics mentioned in 8.4, 
does not exceed the corresponding nmnl)er given in c(^l 3 of Table 2-

A^2. RECOMMENDED CODE OF MANUFACTURE FOR BLANKS 
FOR CONES 

A-2.1 It is recommended that the lin^bor may be converted into 
Straight-grained blatiks of suitable size. However^ a slope of grain not ex- 
ceeding I in 16 should be permitted in the converted blanks. The blanks 
should then be seasoned under proper conditions of drying to the required 
moisture content {see also IS: 1 141-1958* )• The moisture content of 
well-seasoned blanks should not be more than 12 nor less than 8 percent 
at the time of manufacture of cones.
